contact_other_permille.reason: Legion ~100 rounds 1-3 (round 1 protocol 279: one admission per narrow passage, head-on meets near goals, friendly settled bodies stepping aside, long detours at travel speed, ring upkeep and press-in; round 2 protocol 280: sub-cell presses and ring bends, passage lanes, flow-around at travel speed; round 3 on 0.8.6, 2026-10-20: rings round still targets (travel-speed detours, spent closed-off spots by sight test, outer-band waits, flush presses), a passage's green scaled to its crossing and small groups admitted, funnel claims and own-slot arrivals at corridor mouths); bound raised 632 -> 649 at the L100-R3 gate. Before: bound moved 622 -> 632 at the stage-4 gate (inside the stage-3 base's own core-offset spread). stage 4 (protocol 268, 2026-10-16, Legion fair scheduling and budgets): in aware-seen, field work is now served by job (a field, however many groups share it) in four classes -- Waiting, FirstRoute, AwareRepair, StaleRefresh -- each by deficit round robin over a window of its oldest jobs (kWindow 12, kRefreshWindow 3, kSlice 32768) with age promotion, instead of whole quotas to the lowest group id first; a start is admitted oldest first with a bounded fit scan, charges its initialisation (cells/16) to the quota, and the field cap is a fixed byte allowance (128 MiB) instead of 48 whole maps of cells (legion.cpp serveFields, sim/navbudget.h). Before: W9 exit, bound raised 566 -> 622: W9 exit (lane C step C1, decision 7 / W9-U2, protocol 248): the head-on meet of the 16+ columns narrows before contact (aware-unseen click a00 / b00 t90 2162 / 2207 -> 1757 / 1792 against Retail 1877 / 1929; every aware-* click t90 and done is faster; groups' cross contacts pair.contacts fall 4-50x). The aware fixtures' observers are one-body groups, so contact_other counts a body's own click-mates, and the narrowed column packs the click closer (the W3 exit licensed the same cause); the work counters rise by the extra steering of the latched Points (line sweeps, trace cells, still units, slides, slot search) and the completion-distance classes (a body or two settles 1-2 cells further out). Pinned at the exit value.

contact_other_permille.reason: protocol 280 (Legion ~100 round 2, 2026-10-19): a formation member's flow-around shuffle keeps travel speed on a move-like leg (legion.cpp Member::detourFlow; the committed one-cell step round a blocking body crept at the facing cap, an eighth of travel speed sideways), so crowds flow round each other and obstacles sooner: more blocked steps are flowed round (slides) and held between them (holds), bodies press closer (contact) and settle sooner (still-scan samples, completion distances): contact_other_permille 604 at the P280 gate. Was 590: bound moved 585 -> 590 at the stage-8 gate. stage 8 (protocol 272, 2026-10-17, Legion chokepoints, subgroups and arrivals): in aware-unseen, formation members gaining on their own slot, or with a free step toward it, are no longer settled short of it (legion.cpp Member::windowSlotDist, freeTowardSlot): the front of a crowd takes the far side of its area, completions stand nearer their slots (and farther from the click), and in a cramped area the last bodies queue longer instead of settling where they stand. Before: W9 exit, bound raised 483 -> 585: W9 exit (lane C step C1, decision 7 / W9-U2, protocol 248): the head-on meet of the 16+ columns narrows before contact (aware-unseen click a00 / b00 t90 2162 / 2207 -> 1757 / 1792 against Retail 1877 / 1929; every aware-* click t90 and done is faster; groups' cross contacts pair.contacts fall 4-50x). The aware fixtures' observers are one-body groups, so contact_other counts a body's own click-mates, and the narrowed column packs the click closer (the W3 exit licensed the same cause); the work counters rise by the extra steering of the latched Points (line sweeps, trace cells, still units, slides, slot search) and the completion-distance classes (a body or two settles 1-2 cells further out). Pinned at the exit value.

contact_own_permille.reason: Legion ~100 rounds 1-3 (round 1 protocol 279: one admission per narrow passage, head-on meets near goals, friendly settled bodies stepping aside, long detours at travel speed, ring upkeep and press-in; round 2 protocol 280: sub-cell presses and ring bends, passage lanes, flow-around at travel speed; round 3 on 0.8.6, 2026-10-20: rings round still targets (travel-speed detours, spent closed-off spots by sight test, outer-band waits, flush presses), a passage's green scaled to its crossing and small groups admitted, funnel claims and own-slot arrivals at corridor mouths); bound raised 767 -> 784 at the L100-R3 gate. Before: protocol 257 (task-legion-livelock, the 0.8.1 walk-in-place fix): bound moved 758 -> 767 (758 -> 767 (median of the core offsets); the base head's own per-offset range is 568..784). the livelock latch (a body that walked or turned to and fro over a headway window is held: no flow-round, arc or lane pass while it lasts, so the hold's own ways out start) and the side-step guard (no flow straight back after a blocked step toward the arc) change which bodies hold, step aside or yield, so the run takes another course (was: W8 exit, bound raised 744 -> 758: W8 exit (PLAN 3.2 step 2, the passage gate): the door is taken two or three abreast, not in a file (doorplug-124: g.B.done never -> 8042 and g.B.t90 6557 -> 6038 at the gate offsets, stopped 149 -> 115 permille, files 2.50 -> 3.17; doorform done 4011 -> 3827, t90 3557 -> 3467). Bodies abreast are turned by the field at different ticks, which the lane observer counts as swaps after the door (doorplug-124 gate.door.crossings 0 -> 8; doorform reversals 3 -> 8, contact_own 742 -> 758), and the pass scans of a body threading between neighbours rise (pass scan cells 9792 -> 15663 at doorform, 130344 -> 158616 at doorplug-124; line sweeps +4%). Pinned at the exit value.)

work.still_units_processed.max.reason: a work class that did not move here before: stage 4 (protocol 268, 2026-10-16, Legion fair scheduling and budgets): in refreshchurn, its map exceeds 131k cells, so a first footprint-legality plane is no longer built inside the registration that needs it (a whole-map build in one call) but as an incremental job (kPlaneBuildBudget units a tick, legion.cpp planeReady/buildPlanes); the order's registrations wait for it and run in the tick it is ready instead of at command time, so every registration stamp (windows, stall, seed and reseed ticks) moves by at least a tick; and field work is now served by job (a field, however many groups share it) in four classes -- Waiting, FirstRoute, AwareRepair, StaleRefresh -- each by deficit round robin over a window of its oldest jobs (kWindow 12, kRefreshWindow 3, kSlice 32768) with age promotion, instead of whole quotas to the lowest group id first; a start is admitted oldest first with a bounded fit scan, charges its initialisation (cells/16) to the quota, and the field cap is a fixed byte allowance (128 MiB) instead of 48 whole maps of cells (legion.cpp serveFields, sim/navbudget.h). Bodies whose order waits for its plane's first build stand idle meanwhile, so scanStill samples them as still bodies (1 at the stage-4 gate)

g.A.arrived.reason: bound moved 26 -> 22 at the stage-8 gate. stage 8 (protocol 272, 2026-10-17, Legion chokepoints, subgroups and arrivals): in split-450-pocket, formation members gaining on their own slot, or with a free step toward it, are no longer settled short of it (legion.cpp Member::windowSlotDist, freeTowardSlot): the front of a crowd takes the far side of its area, completions stand nearer their slots (and farther from the click), and in a cramped area the last bodies queue longer instead of settling where they stand. Before: bound moved 27 -> 26 at the stage-4 gate (inside the stage-3 base's own core-offset spread). stage 4 (protocol 268, 2026-10-16, Legion fair scheduling and budgets): in split-450-pocket, its map exceeds 131k cells, so a first footprint-legality plane is no longer built inside the registration that needs it (a whole-map build in one call) but as an incremental job (kPlaneBuildBudget units a tick, legion.cpp planeReady/buildPlanes); the order's registrations wait for it and run in the tick it is ready instead of at command time, so every registration stamp (windows, stall, seed and reseed ticks) moves by at least a tick; and field work is now served by job (a field, however many groups share it) in four classes -- Waiting, FirstRoute, AwareRepair, StaleRefresh -- each by deficit round robin over a window of its oldest jobs (kWindow 12, kRefreshWindow 3, kSlice 32768) with age promotion, instead of whole quotas to the lowest group id first; a start is admitted oldest first with a bounded fit scan, charges its initialisation (cells/16) to the quota, and the field cap is a fixed byte allowance (128 MiB) instead of 48 whole maps of cells (legion.cpp serveFields, sim/navbudget.h). Before: bound moved 31 -> 27 at the stage-3 gate. protocol 267 (Legion 10,000 stage 3, explicit selection orders, 2026-10-15): split-450-pocket issues 450 unit commands in one tick (its largest click 450 bodies); the per-unit uplink landed them 64 a tick over 8 ticks, an explicit order lands each click whole in its activation tick, so the bodies start together instead of in 64-body waves. Causal check (docs/legion-10000-progress.md 7.3): the same explicit orders split into 64-member orders landing one a tick reproduce every stage-2 behaviour key exactly on 14 click-heavy fixtures (attackring-mob-100, corner-1x448, cost-corner, deadend-w4-n120-closed-squad/-room-plain, deadend-w6-n120-room-squad, gen1-route-36057, goalblock-200, liftstream, split-450-pocket, strait-3x80, tail-open304, tail-wave, unreach-200; only work totals that include the convoy lookups differ), and split into 64-member orders landing in the SAME tick reproduce this run (deadend-w4/w6-n120): the change is the simultaneous start the brief requires (phase 2: one activation tick per logical order), not the order identity, area or parts.
